task: Write one sentence of your own using the word constrain. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know constrain should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A sprained wrist constrained the pianist to pieces written for the left hand alone.
Limit is the milder, everyday word — a ceiling you bump against; constrain adds the feel of force pressing the bounds in on you.
Immobilize goes further than constrain: what constrains you leaves some room to move, while what immobilizes you leaves none.

Cramp squeezes the room a thing has to work or grow in — a tiny kitchen cramps a cook's style. Constrain is force from outside pressing your options into a narrower set: a rule, an injury, a budget. Cramped, you work awkwardly; constrained, some choices are simply gone.

Bind ties someone down with obligation — a contract, a promise, a duty they cannot shrug off. Constrain presses from outside with no promise involved: weather, budgets, and injuries constrain people who never agreed to anything. You are bound by your word; you are constrained by your circumstances.
